column4: Effects of building materials and structures on radio-wave propagation in the range of 1 MHz to 450 GHz; Application of microwave waveguide techniques for investigating the effect of concrete dielectric and reflection properties during curing
column5: Recommendation ITU-R P.2040-4 (09/2025), Effects of building materials and structures on radio-wave propagation in the range of 1 MHz to 450 GHz. Official PDF: https://www.itu.int/dms_pubrec/itu-r/rec/p/R-REC-P.2040-4-202509-I!!PDF-E.pdf (technical recommendation; not a journal article). Wahab, A., Aziz, M. M. A., MohdSam, A. R., & You, K. Y. (2021). Application of microwave waveguide techniques for investigating the effect of concrete dielectric and reflection properties during curing. Journal of Building Engineering, 38, 102209. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jobe.2021.102209 [SCIE; 2025 JCR Q1; 2025 JIF 8.1; CAS 2025: 2 Top]. Relevance: material dielectric/reflection measurements cover 85 MHz–3.3 GHz. The 3.5 GHz carrier used by the current pipeline is a simulation/evaluation setting, not a value prescribed by this paper.

column4: Surface calibration of electromagnetic properties to simultaneously consider water and chloride contents in concrete both with and without slag; Application of microwave waveguide techniques for investigating the effect of concrete dielectric and reflection properties during curing
column5: El Achrafi, M. K., Villain, G., & Bonnet, S. (2024). Surface calibration of electromagnetic properties to simultaneously consider water and chloride contents in concrete both with and without slag. Construction and Building Materials, 417, 135176. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.conbuildmat.2024.135176 [SCIE; 2025 JCR Q1; 2025 JIF 8.9; CAS 2025: 1 Top]. The paper experimentally characterizes concrete permittivity and resistivity as functions of water/chloride content. Wahab, A., Aziz, M. M. A., MohdSam, A. R., & You, K. Y. (2021). Journal of Building Engineering, 38, 102209. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jobe.2021.102209 [SCIE; 2025 JCR Q1; 2025 JIF 8.1; CAS 2025: 2 Top]. ITU-R P.2040-4, §2.1 and Table 3, provides the frequency-dependent real relative-permittivity model ε′r = a fGHz^b.

column4: Correlation Between the Electromagnetic Properties of Building Materials and Wireless Signal Penetration Loss; Effects of building materials and structures on radio-wave propagation in the range of 1 MHz to 450 GHz
column5: Ayeni, A. A., Yusuf, A., & Onidare, S. (2022). Correlation Between the Electromagnetic Properties of Building Materials and Wireless Signal Penetration Loss. IEEE Transactions on Antennas and Propagation, 70(12), 12040–12048. https://doi.org/10.1109/TAP.2022.3210662 [SCIE; 2025 JCR Q1; 2025 JIF 5.9; CAS 2025: 2 (Engineering, Electrical & Electronic), 1 (Telecommunications)]. The study examines the relationship between building penetration loss and material permittivity/permeability. ITU-R P.2040-4, §2.1.2.1, explicitly treats non-magnetic materials and sets μ = μ0 (therefore μr = 1). This is the assumption adopted by the current Sionna built-in radio-material workflow; non-unit μr is rejected.

column4: Surface calibration of electromagnetic properties to simultaneously consider water and chloride contents in concrete both with and without slag; Measurement and modeling of propagation losses in brick and concrete walls for the 900-MHz band
column5: El Achrafi, M. K., Villain, G., & Bonnet, S. (2024). Construction and Building Materials, 417, 135176. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.conbuildmat.2024.135176 [SCIE; 2025 JCR Q1; 2025 JIF 8.9; CAS 2025: 1 Top]. The paper measures electrical resistivity; conductivity is its reciprocal when the same bulk definition and units are used. Peña, D., Feick, R., Hristov, H. D., & Grote, W. (2003). Measurement and modeling of propagation losses in brick and concrete walls for the 900-MHz band. IEEE Transactions on Antennas and Propagation, 51(1), 31–39. https://doi.org/10.1109/TAP.2003.808539 [SCIE; JCR Q1; 2025 journal JIF 5.9; CAS 2025: 2 (Engineering, Electrical & Electronic), 1 (Telecommunications)]. The paper estimates equivalent ε and σ from empirical wall-transmission data. ITU-R P.2040-4, §2.1 and Table 3, gives σ = c fGHz^d.

column4: A comparison of theoretical and empirical reflection coefficients for typical exterior wall surfaces in a mobile radio environment; Wireless friendliness evaluation and optimisation for sandwich building materials as reflectors
column5: Landron, O., Feuerstein, M. J., & Rappaport, T. S. (1996). A comparison of theoretical and empirical reflection coefficients for typical exterior wall surfaces in a mobile radio environment. IEEE Transactions on Antennas and Propagation, 44(3), 341–351. https://doi.org/10.1109/8.486303 [SCIE; JCR Q1; 2025 journal JIF 5.9; CAS 2025: 2 (Engineering, Electrical & Electronic), 1 (Telecommunications)]. Measurements include brick, glass and limestone surfaces and vertical/horizontal polarizations. Zhang, Y., Zhang, J., Chu, X., & Zhang, J. (2024). Wireless friendliness evaluation and optimisation for sandwich building materials as reflectors. IEEE Transactions on Antennas and Propagation, 72(3), 2697–2711. https://doi.org/10.1109/TAP.2024.3356052 [SCIE; JCR Q1; 2025 journal JIF 5.9; CAS 2025: 2 (Engineering, Electrical & Electronic), 1 (Telecommunications)]. Derives an equivalent reflection coefficient for multilayer building materials. ITU-R P.2040-4, §2.2, defines TE/TM reflection coefficients and single-/multi-layer slab calculations. A reflection coefficient is not itself a dB loss; the chosen power/field definition must be stated.

column4: Measurement and modeling of propagation losses in brick and concrete walls for the 900-MHz band; Measurement of Attenuation by Building Structures in Cellular Network Bands
column5: Peña, D., Feick, R., Hristov, H. D., & Grote, W. (2003). IEEE Transactions on Antennas and Propagation, 51(1), 31–39. https://doi.org/10.1109/TAP.2003.808539 [SCIE; JCR Q1; 2025 journal JIF 5.9; CAS 2025: 2 (Engineering, Electrical & Electronic), 1 (Telecommunications)]. Reports wall-transmission attenuation and estimates equivalent ε/σ for brick and reinforced-concrete walls. Zhekov, S. S., Nazneen, Z., Franek, O., & Pedersen, G. F. (2018). Measurement of Attenuation by Building Structures in Cellular Network Bands. IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters, 17(12), 2260–2263. https://doi.org/10.1109/LAWP.2018.2872620 [SCIE; 2025 JCR Q2; CAS 2025: 2 (Engineering, Electrical & Electronic), 3 (Telecommunications); supplementary polarization-specific measurement]. Tests vertical–vertical and horizontal–horizontal co-polarizations for building structures over 400 MHz–2.7 GHz. ITU-R P.2040-4, §2.2.1–2.2.2, provides TE/TM transmission coefficients and single-/multi-layer slab models.

column4: Influence of diffraction coefficient and corner shape on ray prediction of power and delay spread in urban microcells; Diffraction around corners and its effects on the microcell coverage area in urban and suburban environments
column5: El-Sallabi, H. M., Liang, G., Bertoni, H. L., Rekanos, I. T., & Vainikainen, P. (2002). Influence of diffraction coefficient and corner shape on ray prediction of power and delay spread in urban microcells. IEEE Transactions on Antennas and Propagation, 50(5), 703–712. https://doi.org/10.1109/TAP.2002.1011238 [SCIE; JCR Q1; 2025 journal JIF 5.9; CAS 2025: 2 (Engineering, Electrical & Electronic), 1 (Telecommunications)]. Analyzes building-corner diffraction coefficients and their effects on ray-tracing predictions. Erceg, V., Rustako, A. J., Jr., & Roman, R. S. (1994). Diffraction around corners and its effects on the microcell coverage area in urban and suburban environments at 900 MHz, 2 GHz, and 6 GHz. IEEE Transactions on Vehicular Technology, 43(3), 762–766. https://doi.org/10.1109/25.312770 [SCIE; JCR Q1; 2025 JIF 7.5; CAS 2025: 2]. The detailed incident-min/incident-max/diffracted subfields are retained as the property-set design vocabulary; the current converter does not calculate these dB values.

column1: Screening and interpretation notes: (1) No MDPI journal, conference paper, preprint, book, or ordinary web page is used as a journal reference. (2) ITU-R P.2040-4 is retained as a normative technical recommendation because it is the direct source for the coefficient equations and reflection/transmission theory; it is not counted as an SCI journal paper. (3) The 2025 JCR/CAS indicators are journal-level metrics. IEEE AWPL is included only as supplementary evidence for polarization-specific attenuation and is below the preferred JCR Q1 threshold. (4) The seven properties are conceptual groups; the converter does not currently calculate the three path-loss quantities in dB.
